culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Standards of dress and behaviour are conservative. Respect religious traditions and objects. Respect local restrictions and observances around religious holidays. Full moon (Poya) days are celebrated once a month. Authorities ban the sale and purchase of alcohol and fresh meat on these days. Get local advice before you take photos of places of worship and nearby areas. You may cause offence. Tourism Sri Lanka: at religious sites, cover your shoulders and knees and remove shoes and hats. Ask before photographing people. Don't pose beside Buddha statues or wear Buddha imagery; visible Buddha tattoos have led to deportation.

drone-pilot-pathway.summary: CAASL runs an online drone approval system. Commercial and visitor flights need approval, with Ministry of Defence security clearance; no public operator register was found.

items.text: No public register of drone operators was found on the CAASL drones page. The page does link a list of CAASL-approved UAS importers, manufacturers, assemblers and maintenance organisations (a download).

CAASL's drones page lists an online drone approval system, manual applications, new rules and restricted-area checks, and sets minimum third-party insurance by drone weight (nil up to 0.25 kg, 100,000 rupees from 0.25 to 0.9 kg, rising by weight class). Pilot-licence levels were not read.
For drones brought in by visiting tourists for temporary use, CAASL says the import process does not apply; the visitor instead submits a request for flying approval through CAASL's online portal.
